$comment: Bridge events of the West, 1378 to 1444 (plan-1378 §5 rows Church, Empire, France and England, Iberia, Italy; milestone 10 step 6; EVT-085 to EVT-089, D-EVT-20). Same shape as events-campaign.json's events; the engine joins every events-bridge-<region>.json to the campaign. places: event-tree place -> map provinces, as events-places.json. It also carries six 1444 events re-dated for the 1378 start (same id, replacing the campaign's). Every event is conditional; dates are history, not a script (EVT-004, EVT-019).

localization.event.schism_vincennes.name: France declares for Clement
localization.event.schism_vincennes.desc: At Vincennes in November 1378 Charles V and his council recognise Clement VII, the pope the cardinals elected at Fondi, against Urban VI in Rome. France's choice gives the Avignon pope a kingdom behind him.
localization.event.schism_obedience.name: A realm chooses its Pope
localization.event.schism_obedience.desc: Rome and Avignon each claim the Church. Every Catholic court must say which pope it obeys, and its friends and enemies weigh on the choice: France's allies lean to Avignon, England's to Rome.
localization.event.urban_deposes_joanna.name: Urban deposes Queen Joanna
localization.event.urban_deposes_joanna.desc: Joanna of Naples sheltered the cardinals of Fondi and backs Clement. In 1380 Urban VI declares her deposed and hands her kingdom to her kinsman Charles of Durazzo, a prince of the Hungarian court.
localization.event.wyclif_and_the_lollards.name: Wyclif and the Lollards
localization.event.wyclif_and_the_lollards.desc: John Wyclif attacks the wealth of the Church and the pope's power, and his followers carry an English Bible to the towns. In 1382 a council at Blackfriars condemns his teaching, but the Lollards live on.
localization.event.council_of_pisa.name: The Council of Pisa
localization.event.council_of_pisa.desc: Cardinals of both obediences meet at Pisa in 1409, depose both popes and elect Alexander V. Neither pope gives way, so the Church has three.
localization.event.council_of_constance.name: The Council of Constance
localization.event.council_of_constance.desc: The King of the Romans calls the Church to Constance. The council deposes the Pisan pope and Benedict XIII, accepts Gregory XII's resignation and elects Martin V in 1417. The Western Schism is over.
localization.event.hus_burned.name: Jan Hus burned at Constance
localization.event.hus_burned.desc: Jan Hus preaches Wyclif's reform in Prague. Summoned to the council under a safe-conduct, he is condemned and burned on 6 July 1415, and Bohemia takes his death as an insult to the kingdom.
localization.event.defenestration_of_prague.name: The Defenestration of Prague
localization.event.defenestration_of_prague.desc: In July 1419 Hussites storm Prague's New Town Hall and throw the councillors from the windows. Weeks later King Wenceslaus dies, and Bohemia rises against his heir Sigismund.
localization.event.council_of_basel.name: The Council of Basel
localization.event.council_of_basel.desc: The council that meets at Basel in 1431 claims to stand above the pope. It makes peace with the Hussites, deposes Eugenius IV and elects its own antipope, Felix V, before it dissolves in 1449.
localization.event.union_of_florence.name: The Union of Florence
localization.event.union_of_florence.desc: Hard pressed by the Ottomans, the Byzantine emperor comes to Florence in 1439 and signs a union of the Greek and Latin Churches in return for help. At home the union is hated.
localization.event.wenceslaus_succeeds.name: Wenceslaus succeeds Charles IV
localization.event.wenceslaus_succeeds.desc: Emperor Charles IV dies at Prague on 29 November 1378. His son Wenceslaus, already King of the Romans, follows him without an election, and the Luxembourg lands are shared among the brothers: Sigismund keeps Brandenburg, Jobst Moravia.
localization.event.neuberg_partition.name: The partition of Neuberg
localization.event.neuberg_partition.desc: On 25 September 1379 the Habsburg brothers divide their lands at Neuberg: Albert III keeps Austria, Leopold III takes Styria, Carinthia, Tyrol and the western lands. The house is weaker for a century.
localization.event.swabian_city_war.name: The Swabian City War
localization.event.swabian_city_war.desc: The towns of the Swabian League fight the princes. Count Eberhard of Württemberg breaks their army at Döffingen in 1388, and the Peace of Eger in 1389 forbids the leagues.
localization.event.battle_of_sempach.name: The Battle of Sempach
localization.event.battle_of_sempach.desc: Duke Leopold III marches against Lucerne and its confederates. On 9 July 1386 his knights are cut down at Sempach and the duke is killed.
localization.event.battle_of_naefels.name: The Battle of Näfels
localization.event.battle_of_naefels.desc: In April 1388 the men of Glarus and Schwyz rout a Habsburg army at Näfels. Glarus is free of its Habsburg bailiff and joins the confederates in full.
localization.event.wenceslaus_deposed.name: The deposition of Wenceslaus
localization.event.wenceslaus_deposed.desc: The Rhenish electors meet at Lahnstein in August 1400 and depose King Wenceslaus as idle and useless to the Empire. They elect Rupert of the Palatinate in his place.
localization.event.ruperts_italian_venture.name: Rupert's Italian venture
localization.event.ruperts_italian_venture.desc: Rupert crosses the Alps in 1401 to be crowned in Rome and to humble Gian Galeazzo Visconti. Beaten before Brescia and out of money, he goes home with nothing.
localization.event.sigismund_elected.name: Sigismund King of the Romans
localization.event.sigismund_elected.desc: After Rupert dies in 1410, the electors choose Sigismund, King of Hungary and Wenceslaus's brother. He is the strongest prince of the Empire and means to end the Schism.
localization.event.brandenburg_to_hohenzollern.name: Brandenburg to the Hohenzollerns
localization.event.brandenburg_to_hohenzollern.desc: Sigismund, short of money, pledges and then grants Brandenburg to Frederick, Burgrave of Nuremberg. At Constance in 1415 Frederick is made margrave and elector.
localization.event.saxony_to_the_wettins.name: Saxony to the Wettins
localization.event.saxony_to_the_wettins.desc: The Ascanian electors of Saxe-Wittenberg die out in 1422. Sigismund grants the electorate to Frederick the Warlike of Meissen, and the Wettin lands take the name of Saxony.
localization.event.hussite_crusades.name: The Hussite crusades
localization.event.hussite_crusades.desc: Sigismund leads five crusades into Bohemia between 1420 and 1431. Žižka's wagon forts beat every one, and the war ends only with the Compacts of Basel in 1436.
localization.event.albert_ii_king.name: Albert of Austria takes three crowns
localization.event.albert_ii_king.desc: Sigismund dies in December 1437 without a son. His son-in-law Albert of Austria is chosen King of Hungary and of Bohemia and King of the Romans, the first Habsburg on the throne since 1308.
localization.event.frederick_iii_king.name: Frederick III King of the Romans
localization.event.frederick_iii_king.desc: Albert II dies in 1439 on campaign against the Ottomans. The electors pick his cousin Frederick of Styria, and Hungary chooses Władysław of Poland over Albert's newborn son.
localization.event.brittany_confiscated.name: Brittany confiscated
localization.event.brittany_confiscated.desc: Duke John IV sided with England and fled there. In December 1378 the Parlement declares Brittany forfeit to the crown, and the Breton lords, who wanted no king's rule, call their duke home.
localization.event.death_of_charles_v.name: The uncles' regency
localization.event.death_of_charles_v.desc: Charles V dies on 16 September 1380, leaving an eleven-year-old son. His brothers of Anjou, Berry and Burgundy govern for the boy, empty the treasury, and the hearth tax he abolished on his deathbed brings riots to Paris and Rouen.
localization.event.peasants_revolt.name: The Peasants' Revolt
localization.event.peasants_revolt.desc: The third poll tax to pay for the French war sets Essex and Kent alight in May 1381. Wat Tyler's men take London and kill the chancellor. The boy king Richard meets them at Smithfield, promises freedom, and his council takes it back.
localization.event.richard_ii_deposed.name: Richard II deposed
localization.event.richard_ii_deposed.desc: Richard II exiles and then disinherits his cousin Henry Bolingbroke. Henry lands in 1399 while the king is in Ireland, the lords desert Richard, and Parliament accepts Henry IV. The House of Lancaster needs the French war to prove its right.
localization.event.madness_of_charles_vi.name: The madness of Charles VI
localization.event.madness_of_charles_vi.desc: Riding through the forest of Le Mans in August 1392, Charles VI goes mad and kills four of his own men. For thirty years his fits come and go, and the princes fight over who governs in his name.
localization.event.orleans_murdered.name: The murder of Louis of Orléans
localization.event.orleans_murdered.desc: The king's brother Louis of Orléans and his cousin John the Fearless of Burgundy fight for the council of a mad king. On 23 November 1407 John's men cut Louis down in a Paris street.
localization.event.armagnac_burgundian_war.name: The Armagnac–Burgundian war
localization.event.armagnac_burgundian_war.desc: Orléans's son and his father-in-law Bernard of Armagnac raise the princes against Burgundy. From 1411 France has a civil war inside the English war, and both sides court the English.
localization.event.cabochien_revolt.name: The Cabochien revolt
localization.event.cabochien_revolt.desc: In April 1413 the butchers of Paris, led by Simon Caboche and backed by Burgundy, take the city and force a reform ordinance on the court. The Armagnacs retake Paris in August and tear the ordinance up.
localization.event.battle_of_agincourt.name: The Battle of Agincourt
localization.event.battle_of_agincourt.desc: Henry V renews his claim, takes Harfleur and marches for Calais. On 25 October 1415 his archers destroy the French nobility in the mud at Agincourt. Two years later he begins the conquest of Normandy.
localization.event.treaty_of_troyes.name: The Treaty of Troyes
localization.event.treaty_of_troyes.desc: After John the Fearless is murdered at Montereau, Burgundy joins England. At Troyes on 21 May 1420 the mad Charles VI disinherits his son, makes Henry V his heir and gives him his daughter. English and Burgundian garrisons hold Paris.
localization.event.joan_of_arc.name: Joan of Arc
localization.event.joan_of_arc.desc: In 1429 a peasant girl from Domrémy convinces the Dauphin that God has sent her. She breaks the siege of Orléans in May and brings him to Reims to be crowned. The English burn her at Rouen in 1431, but the tide has turned.
localization.event.congress_of_arras.name: The Congress of Arras
localization.event.congress_of_arras.desc: In September 1435 Philip the Good makes peace with Charles VII at Arras, avenged for his father's murder and freed from homage. The English walk out, and Paris opens its gates to the French king in 1436.
localization.event.ecorcheurs.name: The Écorcheurs
localization.event.ecorcheurs.desc: With the truces, unpaid companies called the Flayers roam Champagne, Burgundy and Alsace. Charles VII's ordinance of 1439 makes the raising of soldiers the king's alone, and in 1445 the best companies become a standing royal army.
localization.event.portuguese_crisis.name: The Portuguese crisis of 1383–85
localization.event.portuguese_crisis.desc: Ferdinand I dies in 1383 and his only child Beatriz is married to John I of Castile. Lisbon rises, the Master of Avis kills the queen's favourite, and the Cortes of Coimbra make him king in 1385.
localization.event.portuguese_crisis.option.avis_take: The Master of Avis is king
localization.event.aljubarrota.name: The Battle of Aljubarrota
localization.event.aljubarrota.desc: John I of Castile invades to take his wife's crown. On 14 August 1385 King John of Avis and Nuno Álvares Pereira, with English archers, destroy his army at Aljubarrota. The Treaty of Windsor binds England and Portugal the next year.
localization.event.lancaster_claim_in_castile.name: Lancaster's claim to Castile
localization.event.lancaster_claim_in_castile.desc: John of Gaunt claims Castile through his wife Constance, daughter of Peter the Cruel. He lands in Galicia in 1386 with Portugal's help, but his army melts away, and at Bayonne in 1388 he sells the claim: his daughter marries the Castilian heir.
localization.event.compromise_of_caspe.name: The Compromise of Caspe
localization.event.compromise_of_caspe.desc: Martin I of Aragon dies in 1410 without an heir. Nine judges meet at Caspe and in June 1412 choose Ferdinand of Antequera, a Castilian Trastámara, over the Count of Urgell. Castile and Aragon now share a dynasty.
localization.event.conquest_of_ceuta.name: The conquest of Ceuta
localization.event.conquest_of_ceuta.desc: On 21 August 1415 John I of Portugal and his sons storm Ceuta across the strait. The first European foothold in Africa gives the princes their knighthood and starts Portugal's turn to the sea.
localization.event.madeira_and_azores.name: Madeira and the Azores
localization.event.madeira_and_azores.desc: Prince Henry's captains settle Madeira from 1420 and find the Azores in 1427. Sugar and wheat from the islands pay for longer voyages south.
localization.event.cape_bojador.name: Past Cape Bojador
localization.event.cape_bojador.desc: Sailors feared the shoals and currents of Cape Bojador as the end of the world. In 1434 Gil Eanes sails past it and comes home, and the West African coast opens to Portuguese ships.
localization.event.alfonso_takes_naples.name: Alfonso V takes Naples
localization.event.alfonso_takes_naples.desc: Joanna II of Naples adopts and then disowns Alfonso V of Aragon. After she dies in 1435 he fights René of Anjou for the kingdom and enters Naples in June 1442, where he keeps his court.
localization.event.war_of_chioggia.name: The War of Chioggia
localization.event.war_of_chioggia.desc: Venice and Genoa fight over Tenedos and the straits. In 1379 the Genoese take Chioggia at the mouth of the lagoon, then are themselves trapped there and surrender in June 1380.
localization.event.peace_of_turin.name: The Peace of Turin
localization.event.peace_of_turin.desc: Amadeus VI of Savoy brokers peace in August 1381. Tenedos is emptied of people and its fort pulled down, and Venice gives up Dalmatia to Hungary.
localization.event.durazzo_takes_naples.name: Charles of Durazzo takes Naples
localization.event.durazzo_takes_naples.desc: With Hungarian troops and Urban's blessing, Charles of Durazzo takes Naples in July 1381 and has Queen Joanna smothered. Joanna had adopted Louis of Anjou, so the Angevins of France now claim the kingdom.
localization.event.gian_galeazzo_coup.name: Gian Galeazzo seizes Milan
localization.event.gian_galeazzo_coup.desc: On 6 May 1385 Gian Galeazzo Visconti, lord of Pavia, rides out to greet his uncle Bernabò outside Milan and arrests him. Bernabò dies in prison, and the Visconti state is one again.
localization.event.milan_made_a_duchy.name: Milan made a duchy
localization.event.milan_made_a_duchy.desc: For 100,000 florins Wenceslaus makes Gian Galeazzo Duke of Milan in 1395, the first duke in Italy by imperial grant. Gian Galeazzo goes on to take Pisa, Siena, Perugia and Bologna.
localization.event.death_of_gian_galeazzo.name: Death of Gian Galeazzo
localization.event.death_of_gian_galeazzo.desc: Gian Galeazzo dies of plague in September 1402 with Florence almost at his mercy. His sons are boys, the condottieri carve up his state, and the threat to Tuscany is gone.
localization.event.florence_takes_pisa.name: Florence takes Pisa
localization.event.florence_takes_pisa.desc: Gian Galeazzo's bastard sells Pisa to Florence in 1405, but the Pisans refuse the sale. Florence besieges the city for a year, and it falls by starvation on 9 October 1406. Florence has its port.
localization.event.ladislaus_of_naples.name: Ladislaus of Naples marches on Rome
localization.event.ladislaus_of_naples.desc: Charles of Durazzo's son Ladislaus uses the Schism to make himself master of the south and takes Rome itself in 1408 and 1413. Florence and the Pisan popes fight him until he dies in 1414.
localization.event.lombard_wars.name: The Lombard wars
localization.event.lombard_wars.desc: Filippo Maria Visconti rebuilds his father's state, and Venice and Florence join against him in 1425. Carmagnola wins Brescia for Venice in 1426 and Bergamo in 1428, and the wars run on for thirty years.
localization.event.sforza_rise.name: Francesco Sforza weds the duke's daughter
localization.event.sforza_rise.desc: Filippo Maria has no son. In 1441 he gives his daughter Bianca Maria to his best condottiere, Francesco Sforza, who will take Milan for himself in 1450. The French house of Orléans keeps its own claim through Valentina Visconti.
